digest.component_or_area: plan-review criterion T1 (overlay-priorart), LLM provider integration
propositions: T1 (a blocking criterion) silently lost web-search grounding when cutover moved from direct Anthropic to Bedrock, because the attachment gate checked provider-name prefix 'anthropic' instead of capability membership
The prefix gate in _anthropic_web_search_capabilities contradicts the epic's zero-exceptions rule that capability decisions derive from registry membership, not name shape

Bedrock does not expose Anthropic's server-side web_search tool in supported_native_tools, so T1 must be served by a rebar-side mechanism (local DuckDuckGo search) to maintain web access on every provider
provider_provenance.capabilities did not record whether web access was attached, making the silent withdrawal unobservable and unable to detect future regressions of this type

plan_review_T1.md framed web access as optional/provider-dependent and included graceful degradation to codebase reasoning, contradicting the operator decision that web access is required for T1 on every provider

Setting constraint kwargs (max_uses, blocked_domains, allowed_domains) at the capability level triggers pydantic-ai's _requires_native() True, suppressing the local fallback and hard-failing on providers without native support — a trap that must not be replicated
